issues.line_text: The victim's identity had been withheld from official reports to protect the family's privacyΓÇösome forums and amateur sleuths had found the first name, but the full details had been kept out of official coverage.

However, the phrasing 'some forums...had found the first name' creates a spoiler riskΓÇösavvy readers might think 'what first name did they find?' and this draws attention to Lily's identity before the reveal. Also, Story Bible confirms Josh researched this case extensively, so claiming forums found 'the first name' is inconsistent with his deep research.
issues.fix: The case details had been carefully controlledΓÇövictim identity withheld to protect the family, no suspects named, minimal information released. The kind of case that frustrated amateur investigators and forum sleuths alike.
issues.rationale: Removes the 'first name found' detail that draws attention to Lily's identity. Maintains Josh's research credibility while keeping victim details vague. Frames it as information control rather than partial leaks.

Eleanor already knew who he was from his podcast announcement 2 years ago (Story Bible: 'She heard Josh announce his Thornewood trip ~2 years ago on his podcast'). issues.line_text: I paused at that entry. An unsolved murderΓÇöexactly the kind of material I'd come here for. The podcast practically wrote itself: atmospheric location, tragic history, questions that never got answers. I made a mental note to dig deeper into the 1998 case.

issues.rationale: Replaces active interest with the trauma avoidance pattern from Story Bible (line 828 consistency fix: 'My eyes kept sliding away from that line'). Josh unconsciously avoids the 1998 case because it's his mother's murder. This prevents drawing attention to 1998 while showing his psychological defense mechanism.

issues.line_text: That left three I couldn't account for. Three that fit the pattern of Thornewood.

notes: Chapter is relatively clean overall. Main issues are: (1) the pseudonym contradiction with Eleanor already knowing his podcast, (2) Josh showing interest in 1998 case when he should be unconsciously avoiding it, (3) timeline claim about Eleanor that needs skepticism, and (4) victim count clarity.
